claim: Known-floor projection is pointwise pinball-nonworsening; true conditional lower inverse quantile has strict breach probability at most alpha, with possible inequality at atoms.
value: Let the forecast-origin information include B, let Y≥B almost surely, and let 0<τ<1. Project any issued report c to max(B,c). Its pinball loss is no larger at every possible Y. A true conditional lower inverse quantile q at level τ=1−α has strict breach probability at most α. Equality is not automatic: an atom at the quantile can make the probability smaller. The lower bound alone need not create an outcome atom; fitted reports do not inherit the population statement.

claim: Exact pinball projection identity and true-quantile strict-tail qualification.
value: \rho_\tau(Y-c)-\rho_\tau(Y-\max\{B,c\})=\tau(B-c)_+,\qquad \Pr(Y>q\mid\mathcal F_t)\le\alpha.

claim: Projection proof and limitation of equality-based coverage diagnostics.
value: Proof. Below B both errors are nonnegative, so their loss difference is the displayed nonnegative quantity; otherwise the report is unchanged. For the conditional inverse quantile, F(q)≥τ, hence the strict-tail probability is at most α. An atom is a possible reason for strict inequality, not a necessary premise. Accordingly, the retained equality-based coverage tests are diagnostics of their stated nulls, not automatic tests of every valid upper quantile.

claim: Classical endpoint-to-peak corollary: independent individually zero-symmetric future real increments, fixed starting anchor, population absolute-displacement quantile.
value: Let future real increments be independent and individually symmetric about zero. Write S<sub>h</sub> for their partial sums, S<sub>0</sub>=0, and fix an observed starting position x with B=|x|. No identical-distribution or finite-moment assumption is required. If q is the population (1−α/2) quantile of |S<sub>H</sub>|, the report B+q has strict peak-breach probability at most α. This is a direct scalar application of the classical Lévy maximal inequality, not a new inequality.

claim: Triangle inclusion, factor-two maximal inequality and correct population quantile bound.
value: \Pr\!\left(\max_{0\le h\le H}|x+S_h|>B+q\right)\le\Pr\!\left(\max_h|S_h|>q\right)\le2\Pr(|S_H|>q)\le\alpha.

claim: Conditional theorem needs conditional premises and conditional population q; empirical overlapping-data plug-in inherits no automatic theorem guarantee.
value: Proof. The triangle inequality gives the first inclusion; Lévy’s maximal inequality and the inverse-quantile tail bound give the rest. For conditional coverage, independence and symmetry must hold conditional on origin information and q must be the corresponding conditional population quantile. The empirical plug-in L, overlapping historical labels and dependent mean-reverting data do not acquire that guarantee. A generic one-sided endpoint VaR is not the required absolute-displacement quantile. Supplement S15 gives an exact finite counterexample to that substitution; Supplement S11 retains the proof, original simulations and corrected sensitivities.

claim: Construction bounds require common history, common available rank, and peaks including the start; no accuracy ordering.
value: Use one nonempty historical pool, one available order-statistic rank k, and peaks that include their starting observation. Let F add historical peak headroom to the current B, S translate each historical signed path to x, and K floor the historical-peak order statistic at B. Their differences obey the following deterministic bounds. The common pool and same rank are essential; these are neither forecast-accuracy nor coverage guarantees.

claim: Exact common-pool anchor-distance inequalities.
value: |F-K|\le r_{\rm abs}=\max_i\bigl||N_i|-B\bigr|,\qquad |S-K|\le r_{\rm signed}=\max_i|N_i-x|.
